ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a parallelogram ABCD, A is at the upper left, B is at the upper right, C is at the lower right, D is at the lower left. Side AB and DC are parallel, side AD and BC are parallel. In the figure, the interior angle 115° is marked at vertex A, the right side BC is labeled 18, and the bottom side DC is labeled 12. The problem asks to find m∠ADC, that is, the interior angle at vertex D. Reasoning: In a parallelogram, adjacent interior angles are supplementary. ∠DAB and ∠ADC are adjacent angles, therefore m∠DAB + m∠ADC = 180°. It is known that m∠DAB = 115°, so m∠ADC = 180° - 115° = 65°.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: ABCD is drawn as a parallelogram with vertices A top-left, B top-right, C bottom-right, D bottom-left, and the interior angle at A is labeled 115°. The question asks for m∠ADC, the interior angle at D. Use the parallelogram property that consecutive interior angles are supplementary because opposite sides AB and DC are parallel and AD is a transversal. Therefore ∠A + ∠D = 180°, so m∠ADC = 180° - 115° = 65°.
